title: tx_queue.c: pthread_mutex_init return value ignored (UB risk)
description: Line 217: pthread_mutex_init() can fail with EAGAIN or ENOMEM but the return value is not checked. The function returns 0 (success) unconditionally. Subsequent pthread_mutex_lock() calls on an uninitialized mutex cause undefined behavior - deadlocks, crashes, or memory corruption.
close_reason: Fix verified present in current working tree (UNCOMMITTED — must be included in next commit): tx_queue.c tx_queue_init() POSIX branch now does 'int err = pthread_mutex_init(&queue->lock, NULL); if (err != 0) { return -err; }' (lines 215-218). Defect still exists at HEAD (git show HEAD confirms unchecked init); the fix arrived in an earlier session's uncommitted diff. Verification: host cmake build of lichen/tests/tx_queue (-Wall -Wextra -Werror) passes, full suite 22/22 OK; TSAN build runs clean. Error propagation matches tx_queue_destroy() convention (-err).
